integrated_multimodal_description: [Shot 1] A brisk ten-second LIVE-ACTION fight, continuous at normal speed. Preserve the exact two human actors, faces, black hair, costumes, proportions, wrapped tail and warm rocky canyon from Picture1. Goku is the orange/blue actor initially on the LEFT. Vegeta is the navy/white/gold armored actor initially on the RIGHT. The supplied paired BODY MOTION CONTROL determines the trajectories, actor positions, rapid arm withdrawal, kick arcs and separate supporting footfalls. Render human flesh, gloves, cloth and boots around those moving bodies; never draw the control lines or copy its black background.

Use the motion timing rather than stretching a punch across a whole time range. A strike is one quick out-and-back action: the fist or shin touches momentarily, IMMEDIATELY separates and returns while the struck body continues recoiling. Hands never remain stuck to the other fighter's arm, glove, face or torso. No grappling, hand-holding or sustained pushing. Weight comes from the defender's torso and pelvis being driven off their original base, followed by a forced catching step and a second settling step.

Opening0.0-0.6s: Vegeta briskly pulls the anchor's extended right glove back to his cheek. Both close distance with separate grounded fighting steps, following the body guide. Do not hold the opening photograph. The next attack starts from the chambered glove.

Follow the linked motion: Vegeta drives a sharp RIGHT body punch around0.73s; Goku folds and is pushed backward into a catching step after contact. Goku recovers and snaps a LEFT straight toward Vegeta's head around2.06s, then withdraws; Vegeta's head/trunk recoil and his boots catch his backward weight. Goku's RIGHT low kick reaches Vegeta's thigh around4.11s and immediately recoils; Vegeta's struck base gives way into a lateral step. Goku snaps a short LEFT punch at the guard around5.0s and retracts; the blocked impulse is smaller. Continue the intervening short boxing footwork and parries in the body guide.

Vegeta regains initiative with a LEFT front kick to Goku's torso around7.63s; his RIGHT support boot stays on the ground, his kicking knee bends to withdraw and his left foot lands promptly. Goku's trunk and hips travel away from the contact and his feet take distinct hurried recovery steps. Vegeta follows with a short LEFT jab into the recovering guard around8.54s and a sharp RIGHT straight toward the head around9.40s; each glove snaps back separately. Goku's last recoil and lowered catch stance carry through the end. No reset to the opening photograph.

The camera follows the continuous circling footwork with a smooth physical tracking/orbit that keeps the two bodies separated in a three-quarter side view. It remains on the same relative side of their moving attack line; no cut, shake or fast zoom hides a contact. Keep heads, hands and both pairs of boots inside frame. One consistent ground surface and daylight direction. A support sole stays planted while the other foot steps; boots lift, travel and land individually, never hover together or slide as one rigid object. Knees and hips absorb the displaced weight. Cloth and dust react after actual body motion and boot landings.

Fast compact strikes, normal human coordination, tangible mass. No slow motion, speed ramps, held contact, drifting airborne stance, extra people, duplicated or fused limbs, energy powers, transformations, blood, new wounds, captions or text.

overall_soundscape: Silent visual diagnostic. No voices, screams, grunts, Foley, music or ambience.

non_diegetic_music: None.

[Human realism direction]
Preserve the reference identity, age, facial proportions, skin tone, costume and lighting. Natural skin microtexture, subtle pores, varied roughness and realistic highlights; natural eyes, muscle tension and expressions. Avoid waxy or plastic skin, beauty smoothing and airbrushed faces. Preserve the requested camera behavior; realism does not require camera shake.

[Combat physical direction]
Execute only the specified choreography, attacks, defenses, powers and outcome. Preserve each actor's identity, weapon ownership, geography and accumulated damage. Physical chain for every exchange: anticipation, ground-supported propulsion through legs and hips, trajectory, visible contact or evasion, momentum transfer, displacement, reaction, recovery. A block redirects momentum; a miss carries inertia. Balance, friction, traction, gravity and center of mass govern motion. Reactions caused by impacts start after contact; anticipatory defenses remain allowed. Feet step, pivot, skid or drag visibly, never slide rigidly. Grapples require grip, tension and leverage; jumps require compression, takeoff, ballistic travel and landing. Cloth, hair and loose material follow bodies with delayed secondary motion; environmental response follows the impact. Keep attack lines, contact and body displacement readable in the requested camera. Continue motion between actions without automatic guard resets, freeze poses, teleporting, limb fusion or interpenetration. No artificial slow motion or speed ramps unless requested. No flashes, cuts or camera shake to conceal missing contact. Finish requested attacks before any subsequent dialogue, preserving the exact dialogue and requested audio. Do not invent extra opponents, injuries, dialogue or soundtracks. Follow the requested intensity and the character's established abilities.
